title: PE03 Borrower Evidence Reading Lab
placement: Supplemental public practice within existing PE03 Units 3A–3C; not a ninth module
access_and_scope: Free public self-guided practice before, during, and after paid enrollment. No account or payment is required.
Under construction. Not NMLS approved. No credit, education hours, certificate, license, SAFE test result, or course-completion determination is awarded. This lab adds no proposed or earned minutes.
All case records, entities, labels, amounts, tasks, and case decisions are original fictional teaching material. Do not enter or upload real borrower records or identifying information.
These are simplified training records, not complete underwriting evidence, lender forms, or legal advice. No real account numbers, Social Security numbers, logos, or copied lender forms are used.
Every answer, derivation, and rubric is intentionally public formative feedback. No protected examination, private instructor guide, private case key, or protected item bank was used.

The fictional case reviewer is an authored role in the case, not a course instructor. This lab provides no instructor replies, simulated peer exchanges, or actual online instructor led (OIL) delivery. Self-review does not satisfy the genuine interaction and instructor-feedback requirements of a future OIL offering.
learning_goals: Extract facts from the actual fields of a training record before using a summary.
Separate reported amounts, arithmetic estimates, and accepted case inputs.
Read payment frequency, gross and net earnings, variable earnings, period coverage, and missing pages.
Reconcile asset balances without counting an inter-account transfer as new money.
Distinguish requested, received, reviewed, and accepted evidence.
Preserve source facts and prior answers when a later record changes the analysis.
working_instructions: Keep an offline response sheet. For each task save the task ID, branch, version, source IDs and fields, first answer, revised answer, and reason for revision. Do not overwrite the first answer.

Work through the five releases in order. All releases and public feedback are visible; the sequence is a reading discipline, not a timed or credit-bearing gate. Try a task before reading its feedback.

At Release 2 choose Branch R (missing page later received) or Branch U (page still unavailable). Both are valid case paths. Keep that choice throughout; compare the other path only as a separately labeled alternative.
Branch R alone receives E06. Branch U must not borrow E06 evidence. Both paths receive E07–E10. E07 states separate asset inputs for each path. The later debt change applies to both paths.

Use the reviewer’s accepted inputs for qualification calculations and funds-availability decisions. Other tasks expressly ask for arithmetic on reported, observed, estimated, or provisional facts; perform that arithmetic and label its source and status clearly without presenting it as accepted. Do not infer an approval, denial, or universal program limit from an answer.

Use dollars and cents for currency. Keep full precision until the final operation; display percentages to two decimals. A change between percentages is reported in percentage points. There are 12 months in the annual-to-monthly conversions.
Dates within the fictional file describe its chronology. Release numbers describe when the learner sees a record, so an earlier-dated record can appear in a later release.

reading_aids.title: Read a pay record in this order
reading_aids.text: Identify the creator and the person it concerns, the pay period, payment date, stated pay frequency, current base and additional earnings, gross total, deductions, net amount, and year-to-date columns. Current and year-to-date columns measure different periods. A bank deposit is usually a net cash receipt; do not substitute it for gross qualifying income.

reading_aids.title: Read a bank record in this order
reading_aids.text: Locate the holder, symbolic account label, statement period, page count, opening and closing balances, and transaction details. A missing page is a specific evidence gap even when the displayed totals balance. Add ending balances from the same date; do not then add the transfers already reflected in them.

reading_aids.title: Four states answer four different questions
reading_aids.text: Requested: what was asked for? Received: what arrived and when? Reviewed: who examined it, and for what purpose? Accepted: who had authority to decide that a stated requirement was met? A completeness review can identify a missing page without accepting the assets. Track these events separately, not as interchangeable labels.

reading_aids.title: Separate three kinds of statement
reading_aids.text: A source fact is a field in an exhibit. A derived result is arithmetic using identified fields. An accepted input is a case-specific decision expressly supplied by the fictional reviewer. The source notes below contain legal or program concepts; they do not turn a fictional reviewer choice into a rule.

sources.title: Standards for Employment and Income Documentation
sources.scope: Fannie Mae employment-income documentation; not a universal legal rule or a complete checklist.
sources.concept: Borrower-provided employment records must identify their third-party source and be complete and legible. A paystub needs enough information for the income calculation, including year-to-date earnings. A borrower upload does not change who originated the record.

sources.title: Base Income
sources.scope: Fannie Mae base-income treatment. Overtime is a separate income category; this lab supplies no overtime-eligibility method.
sources.concept: For fixed base pay, biweekly gross pay is converted using 26 payments divided by 12 months; twice-monthly pay uses two payments per month. The Guide also distinguishes fixed from variable base income and calls for consistency with year-to-date base earnings. This calculation alone does not establish eligibility.

sources.title: Depository Accounts
sources.scope: Fannie Mae depository assets. This lab does not teach large-deposit thresholds, all verification alternatives, or an account-exclusion rule.
sources.concept: Funds used for a down payment, closing costs, or reserves must be verified. A transfer whose source is identifiable on statements between verified accounts can be treated differently from an unexplained deposit. Indications of borrowed funds still require attention.

sources.authority: CFPB Regulation Z and official interpretations
sources.title: Minimum standards for transactions secured by a dwelling
sources.scope: Covered ability-to-repay determinations; the regulation contains exceptions and requirements not reproduced here.
sources.concept: For covered transactions, income or assets relied on must be verified with reasonably reliable third-party records, subject to the regulation. The official interpretation of paragraph (c)(7) does not prescribe one specific DTI limit. A computed ratio alone therefore does not decide this case.

source_scope_note: The linked primary pages were read on October 1, 2026. Page revision dates differ from this verification date and from any applicable effective date. Check current law, program instructions, transaction coverage, and lender authority before using a real file. The concise concepts above support document-reading habits; they are not a whole underwriting policy. All amounts and reviewer decisions below are fictional case facts, not facts taken from these sources.

branches.title: Missing page received
branches.condition: The checking transaction page E06 arrives on September 18.

branches.title: Missing page unavailable
branches.condition: The checking transaction page has not arrived at any point in this path.

stages.title: Read the original packet
stages.instruction: Use only E01–E04. No acceptance decision has yet been supplied.

stages.title: Request the exact missing evidence
stages.instruction: Choose R or U now and record the choice. The page is still missing in both paths at this release.

stages.title: Reconcile and calculate under supplied decisions
stages.instruction: Read E06 only in R. Read the correct R or U asset instruction in E07. Save the resulting V1-reviewed analysis before continuing.

stages.title: Receive a changed debt fact
stages.instruction: Preserve V1-reviewed. Record the new evidence without pretending it was known or accepted earlier.

stages.title: Recalculate after the case review
stages.instruction: Use E10 only now. Save the revised calculation beside the original and explain the change.

exhibits.warning: FICTIONAL EXCERPT — Simplified training record, not complete underwriting evidence.

fields.employment: Fixed salary at Training Workshop — fictional employer

No income, assets, occupancy classification, or loan decision is accepted merely because it appears in A1.

exhibits.warning: FICTIONAL EXCERPT — Simplified training record, not complete underwriting evidence.

Reconcile A1 twice-monthly calculation with P1 biweekly pay frequency
Program-appropriate overtime history and review; no acceptable history has yet been supplied

exhibits.kind: supplement to E03, Branch R only

The new creditor record is accepted as an included $180 payment solely by this supplied September 23 memo. It was not accepted in the September 22 receipt log.

tasks.title: Build the reported borrower snapshot
tasks.prompt: Before reading any reviewer memo, write a six-line snapshot naming the applicant label, transaction purpose and reported occupancy intent, employment source, reported base and overtime, reported assets, and reported nonhousing payments. Recompute the reported income and funds totals. Label each line reported rather than verified or accepted.

public_self_review.explanation: A1 reports a purchase with principal-residence intent, fixed salary from Training Workshop, $6,000 base plus $600 overtime, and $700 nonhousing payments. Its income total is $6,600. Its funds total is $31,000 only because it adds a $4,000 transfer to $17,000 checking and $10,000 savings; that is the applicant’s report to investigate, not an accepted asset amount.
rubric: Names E01 as an applicant-originated source
Labels intent and amounts reported
Reproduces the transfer as part of the original report without endorsing it

tasks.title: Read the pay statement columns
tasks.prompt: Extract the pay period, pay date, frequency, current base, overtime, gross, deductions, net, and year-to-date base. Identify the record creator and uploader separately. Check the current gross-to-net arithmetic and the year-to-date base against the number of pay events. Explain why the net column is not the same measure as gross base pay.

public_self_review.explanation: P1 covers August 24–September 6 and pays September 11, biweekly. Payroll created it; the applicant uploaded it. Current base $3,000 plus overtime $240 gives $3,240 gross. Deductions of $800, $200, and $140 total $1,140, leaving $2,100 net. Eighteen base payments of $3,000 reconcile to $54,000 year-to-date base. These cross-checks inspect internal consistency; they do not establish full income eligibility.
rubric: Keeps pay period distinct from payment date
Separates base, overtime, gross, deductions, and net
Uses the current column for the current check and the year-to-date column for cumulative pay
Does not describe applicant upload as applicant-created payroll

tasks.title: Resolve the pay-frequency mismatch
tasks.prompt: Convert only P1 fixed gross base pay to a monthly arithmetic estimate using its stated frequency. Compare it with A1 reported base. Then calculate the monthly figure someone would obtain by mistakenly using P1 net pay with the same frequency. Label that second answer a net-cash extrapolation, not accepted qualifying income. State what still requires review.

public_self_review.explanation: Base conversion: $3,000 × 26 ÷ 12 = $6,500, which is $500 above A1 base. Using two payments every month would reproduce A1’s $6,000 and miss two annual payments. Net extrapolation gives $4,550, but it mixes take-home cash with the gross-income calculation. Frequency and base arithmetic can be reconciled; actual income acceptance awaits the appropriate review.
rubric: Uses 26, not 24, annual pay periods
Excludes overtime from the base conversion
Distinguishes an arithmetic estimate from a qualifying-income decision
Keeps the original $6,000 report visible

tasks.title: Keep variable earnings unresolved
tasks.prompt: A colleague proposes multiplying the current $240 overtime by 26 and dividing by 12. Compute that figure, compare it with the $600 report, and write two sentences explaining why neither amount has yet become accepted overtime. Identify a focused next evidence-and-review need without inventing a required history length.

public_self_review.explanation: The one-check extrapolation is $520 per month, $80 below the report. That difference is not evidence that either number is a supported qualifying amount. The packet has a current payment and a cumulative year-to-date total, but no supplied decision accepting a representative overtime history. Request the history and applicable income review; do not choose the larger figure merely to lower DTI. This lab intentionally does not teach a complete overtime policy.
rubric: Labels $520 an extrapolation only
Separates overtime from fixed base pay
Requests program-appropriate history and analysis without inventing a universal period
Does not infer accepted overtime from a single check

tasks.title: Audit the received packet
tasks.prompt: Create one inventory line for each record: period, expected pages, received pages, exact gap, and present review status. Check the checking-summary and savings-summary equations. Explain why a balanced summary and an uploaded file do not establish acceptance. Do not invent a requested or reviewed date that has not appeared yet.

public_self_review.explanation: P1 supplies modeled pages 1–2; C1 supplies 1 and 3 of 3 and lacks page 2; S1 supplies 1–2. All were received September 16. At Release 1 no review or acceptance event has been supplied. Checking: $16,000 + $8,200 − $7,200 = $17,000. Savings: $14,000 − $4,000 = $10,000. Equations can agree while transaction evidence remains missing.
rubric: Names C1 page 2 and August 2026 specifically
Separates complete modeled page sets from complete underwriting evidence
Marks review and acceptance not yet established
Does not fill missing transaction detail by assumption

tasks.title: Inventory balances without inventing availability
tasks.prompt: Add the two August 31 ending balances once. Compare the result with A1 reported funds. Explain the likely double-counting issue while stating which matching transfer evidence is still missing. Can this calculation yet be called accepted funds to close?

public_self_review.explanation: The displayed balances total $27,000, $4,000 below A1’s $31,000. Adding a transfer as extra funds on top of ending balances risks counting the same money again. S1 shows a transfer out, but the matching checking transaction page is still absent. The $27,000 is a combined displayed balance, not accepted funds at this release.
rubric: Uses balances with the same August 31 date
Does not add the transfer to ending balances
States the checking-side evidence gap
Keeps displayed balances distinct from eligible or accepted assets

tasks.title: Track four evidence states
tasks.prompt: Choose Branch R or U and record it. At the end of Release 2, make a four-state log for P1, C1 missing page 2, and the overtime history. For each, distinguish request, receipt, review purpose, and acceptance. Replace the inaccurate label “all uploads verified” with one accurate sentence.

public_self_review.explanation: P1 was received September 16 and checked September 17 for completeness and a frequency conflict; qualifying income is not yet accepted. C1 page 2 was requested September 17 but is not yet received in either path. Overtime history was requested September 17 and remains unreceived and unaccepted. A defensible status says: “Original records received; checking page 2 and overtime history remain requested, and qualification review remains outstanding.”
rubric: Records R or U explicitly
Does not advance R receipt to September 17
Names the limited completeness review rather than calling it underwriting acceptance
Uses separate requested and received states

tasks.title: Write a precise evidence request
tasks.prompt: Draft a two- or three-sentence request to the fictional applicant about the missing bank page. Identify the account label, period, received pages, missing page, purpose, and secure channel. Avoid asking again for pages already received or promising an approval. This is writing practice; send nothing.

public_self_review.explanation: Example: “We have pages 1 and 3 of your August 2026 TRAIN-CHECK statement. Please provide page 2 through the secure portal so the complete record can be reviewed; if that page is unavailable, let the review team know so it can identify an acceptable alternative.” Equivalent neutral wording is welcome. A precise request explains the evidence gap without claiming a credit outcome.
rubric: Identifies August 2026 TRAIN-CHECK page 2
Acknowledges pages 1 and 3 already received
Uses the fictional secure portal, with no real upload
Routes alternatives to the responsible reviewer and makes no approval promise

tasks.title: Build the source-to-fact map
tasks.prompt: For your selected branch, build eight rows: pay frequency, reported base, accepted base, reported overtime, included overtime, checking funds, savings funds, and original nonhousing payments. Record the exact exhibit field, period or decision date, receipt date, review or acceptance scope, current value, and open question. Keep the original report beside the accepted input. In U do not cite E06 as received evidence.

public_self_review.explanation: A useful map separates A1’s $6,000 report from M1’s accepted $6,500 and separates reported overtime $600 from included overtime $0 with history unresolved. Checking is a displayed $17,000 in both paths; M1 accepts $17,000 only in R and $0 in U. M1 accepts savings $10,000 in either path. E08 lists the three original debt payments, and M1 supplies their inclusion. The public map below gives one model; equivalent source-linked records are acceptable.
rubric: Includes all eight facts with sources and dates
Preserves report versus accepted input
Attributes acceptance to fictional M1, not the learner or an instructor
Carries the branch-specific checking condition
Uses an open question instead of an invented resolution

tasks.title: Trace the transfer on the chosen path
tasks.prompt: R: total E06 credits and debits, match its transfer to E04, and reconcile the combined account opening and closing balances using only external inflows and outflows. U: state which transaction-level reconciliation cannot be done, then calculate the gap between combined displayed balances and M1 accepted assets. If you compare paths, keep two separately labeled answers.

public_self_review.explanation: R credits are $2,100 + $4,000 + $2,100 = $8,200. Debits total $7,200. Across both accounts, the $4,000 transfer out and in cancel; $30,000 opening balances + $4,200 external payroll − $7,200 external outflows = $27,000 closing balances. U lacks E06 and cannot verify the checking transaction match. U displayed balances of $27,000 exceed supplied accepted assets of $10,000 by $17,000; that gap is unresolved checking, not proof that the money disappeared.
rubric: R matches date, amount, and symbolic account labels on both sides
R excludes the internal transfer from new external funds
U does not use E06
Keeps asset acceptance sourced to M1

tasks.title: Calculate the original qualification measures
tasks.prompt: For V1-reviewed, total all five M1 housing components and all three D1 payments. Use M1 accepted income, show the numerator and denominator, and calculate the housing ratio and total DTI. In R only, use E06 to explain why its existing $1,600 housing outflow does not replace M1 proposed qualifying housing. In U, do not use E06; explain generally why a bank outflow, if later documented, would not by itself replace an accepted M1 input. In either path, explain why net pay and reported overtime do not replace the supplied income. Both paths use the same accepted income and debt inputs here.

public_self_review.explanation: M1 housing totals $2,450. D1 other payments total $700. Accepted income is $6,500 base plus $0 overtime = $6,500. Housing ratio is $2,450 ÷ $6,500 × 100 = 37.69%. Total DTI is ($2,450 + $700) ÷ $6,500 × 100 = 48.46%. In R, E06’s $1,600 bank outflow describes prior cash movement; M1 specifies proposed qualifying housing. U cannot cite that missing page or its transaction amount; it can explain that a cash-flow observation alone would not change the accepted M1 housing input. In either path, net cash and unresolved reported overtime are different measures. No threshold has been supplied.
rubric: Lists all five housing components and all three debt payments
Uses $6,500 accepted income
Shows the full DTI numerator
Does not turn the percentage into approval or denial
Uses E06 and the $1,600 observation only in R; U gives a general explanation without claiming receipt of that page

tasks.title: Separate funds to close from reserves
tasks.prompt: For your chosen path, compare M1 accepted assets with the remaining $22,000 needed to close and the separate $3,000 case reserve target. R: calculate funds left after closing and surplus above the reserve target. U: calculate the cash-to-close shortfall and the total additional eligible funds needed to cover both closing and the target. Do not call a negative balance reserves. Describe the other path separately if you compare it.

public_self_review.explanation: R: $27,000 − $22,000 = $5,000 left; subtract the $3,000 target and the surplus is $2,000. U: $22,000 − $10,000 = $12,000 needed just to cover closing; covering closing plus $3,000 reserves needs $15,000 additional eligible funds. U cannot complete the assumed closing with current accepted assets, so a negative “reserve balance” is misleading. These outcomes address the supplied cash assumptions only.
rubric: Uses only the selected branch asset total
Does not reuse closing funds as reserves
Labels U $12,000 as closing shortfall and $15,000 as combined funding gap
States that $3,000 is a fictional case target

tasks.title: Explain the limited decision
tasks.prompt: Write a three-sentence status for the fictional applicant. Include one accepted input, the result under your branch, one unresolved issue, and the responsible review function. Correct the statement “The DTI result proves this loan is approved.” Distinguish a case assumption from a program or legal fact.

public_self_review.explanation: A strong R answer can say that the supplied review uses $6,500 income and $27,000 assets, with $5,000 left after the assumed closing and a 48.46% DTI calculation; the overtime request remains unresolved, and this packet gives no final loan decision. A strong U answer uses only $10,000 accepted assets and identifies the missing checking page and review, a $12,000 closing shortfall, and no final decision. The fictional reviewer owns acceptance; the learner reports and routes. The reserve target is a case choice. S04 explains why its covered rule does not itself supply one universal DTI cutoff.
rubric: Makes the selected branch unambiguous
Names a real open issue in the fictional file
Separates mathematical results from loan approval
Does not invent instructor assessment or a program threshold

tasks.title: Record a changed fact before acceptance
tasks.prompt: Start a changed-fact log without altering V1-reviewed. Record the old fact and its source date, the new obligation and its source/receipt dates, what could change, present status, next decision owner, and your preserved response version. Calculate the provisional new nonhousing-payment total, clearly labeled pending review. Explain why the earlier debt record does not cancel the newer evidence.

public_self_review.explanation: D1 as of September 17 supports the original $700. D2 dated September 21, received September 22, adds a $180 payment and replaces none of the old debts. The potential total is $880, pending the supplied authorized review. Mark V2-pending; preserve V1-reviewed and the original 48.46% result as historical. Route income/debt calculation effects to the authorized underwriting review function. Receipt alone does not yet establish the new accepted-input decision.
rubric: Separates source date, receipt date, and decision date
Keeps the first calculation unchanged as historical
Labels $880 provisional
Identifies re-review without assuming it already occurred

tasks.title: Recalculate from the versioned decision
tasks.prompt: After reading M2, finish V2-reviewed: recompute accepted total nonhousing payments, total DTI numerator, and DTI. Calculate the percentage-point change from V1 using unrounded ratios. Add the acceptance date and source to the changed-fact log. State whether the cash analysis changes under the supplied assumptions and whether A2 reported overtime is now accepted.

public_self_review.explanation: M2 on September 23 includes $180 in addition to the original $700, giving $880 nonhousing payments. $2,450 + $880 = $3,330; $3,330 ÷ $6,500 × 100 = 51.23%. Compared with $3,150 ÷ $6,500 × 100, the increase is 2.77 percentage points. M2 expressly keeps the branch assets, cash-to-close, reserve target, housing, and accepted income unchanged. The cash analysis remains the same; $600 reported overtime still contributes $0 to qualifying income. No new loan approval follows from this arithmetic.
rubric: Uses September 23 as the supplied acceptance date
Includes both old and new debt
Calculates percentage-point change from unrounded values
Keeps U checking unresolved and both branches separate
Preserves reported versus included overtime

tasks.title: Write and revise an evidence handoff
tasks.prompt: Write a 120–180-word handoff for the responsible fictional review team using your branch. Cite at least four exhibit IDs. Explain the corrected base-pay frequency, reported versus included overtime, the transfer and branch asset status, the changed debt and revised DTI, and the unresolved decision boundary. Name one linked primary-source concept and one fictional case assumption separately. Compare your handoff with the public rubric, retain the first version, and write a revision plus one sentence explaining what changed or why no change was warranted.

public_self_review.explanation: There is no single required wording. A complete handoff makes the evidence trail reproducible and keeps limits visible: $6,500 accepted base; $600 reported overtime with $0 included; balances $27,000 without an extra transfer; branch R accepted $27,000 or branch U accepted $10,000 with checking unresolved; $880 current nonhousing payments; DTI revised from 48.46% to 51.23% following M2. It distinguishes legal/program guidance from the fictional $3,000 reserve target and closes with the actual open review need, not a funding promise. Self-review and revision are learning activities, not a pass result or instructor assessment.
rubric: Cites at least four relevant exhibits rather than relying on an unsupported summary
Explains frequency, gross versus net, and unresolved overtime
